title: Capacity Flex Bundles: tokenized GPU overage & tiered-latency SLA pilot
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Validate a 'Capacity Flex Bundle' product that combines reserved GPU capacity with a tokenized on-demand overage mechanism and discrete latency SLA tiers. This ticket defines the pilot plan to test two commercial constructs (Tokenized Overage vs. Flat Burst Fee) plus three SLA latency tiers (Standard/Plus/Prime) against a set of enterprise prospects and internal workloads. We need deterministic billing semantics for legal, clear UX in the Console, and contract language for Dedicated agreements that references the addendum and audit log requirements.
background: Sales feedback in Q4 2025 indicated customers want predictable committed capacity but dislike large unused commits and want cheap, rapid bursts for spiky inference. Existing reserved models (commit + burst credits) are frictional in procurement and accounting. The idea: sell smaller reserved pools + buy 'burst tokens' (micro-units proportional to GPU-seconds) or a simple monthly flat burst allowance. We also want to offer SLA tiers tied to provisioning priority and latency SLOs to capture premium willingness-to-pay.
plan: Design two pricing arms: A) Tokenized Overage: tokens sold in packs (1 token = 1 GPU-second at baseline price) with volume discounts; B) Flat Burst Fee: monthly add-on allowing N minutes of burst at x% of reserved capacity.
Define three SLA tiers and operational guarantees: Standard (99.5% p95 latency), Plus (99.8% p95), Prime (99.95% p95) with associated priority routing and preemptible fallback rules.
Create legal addendum draft (billing annex + audit log clause + data isolation statement) and send to Legal for review. Include example invoice line items and reconciliation rules.
Implement Console UX mockups: billing page, burst purchase flow, quota UI, and per-route SLA selector; link to design review in Confluence.
Run a 6-week pilot with 5 customers (mix of AI-native startups and mid-market) and 3 internal Redwood workloads to gather telemetry and invoice reconciliation data.
A/B test pricing arms across pilot customers (randomized by cohort) and collect conversion, usage patterns, and NPS impact.
Measure cost exposure scenarios across our GPU fleet and develop a risk-capacity buffer policy for Dedicated capacity pools.
Finalize recommended public SKUs and launch plan (beta -> GA) based on pilot outcomes and legal signoff.
acceptance_criteria: Legal has approved the billing addendum language and audit log requirements (or provided a tracked change set).
Console mockups reviewed & approved by Design and Engineering with implementation plan and story estimate.
Pilot telemetry collected: per-customer daily token consumption, burst event latency, and reserved utilization summaries for 6 weeks.
Decision criteria recorded: one pricing arm selected or recommendation to iterate, plus recommended price points and SLA premiums.
Pricing sensitivity analysis showing expected ARR uplift and downside scenarios (P50/P90 cost exposure) attached.
Minimum of 3 pilot participants confirm willingness to sign the addendum or convert to a beta SKU at proposed pricing.
metrics: Average token burn per customer per burst event
Churn risk delta for customers offered Flex Bundles vs baseline
SLA attainment by tier: target p95 latency meet rate >= defined percentage per tier
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tokenized Overage gives fine-grained billing but increases invoicing complexity and customer accounting overhead. Flat Burst Fee is simpler but may leave revenue on the table for high-burst customers. SLA tiers increase ops complexity and require priority routing heuristics—risk of customer dissatisfaction if fallbacks trigger. Fleet risk: unbounded bursts could overload physical pools; we will implement a buffer policy and explicit hard caps for Dedicated.
